pictures.scene: King David Kneeling before an Altar — the king down on one knee in his crown and armour under a heavy gold cope worked with little scenes, one hand laid flat on his breast and his face turned up, the harp standing beside him and an angel sweeping in above, for the choirmaster according to Sheminith a Psalm of David, help O LORD for the godly are no more
pictures.name: pd_king_david_kneeling_before_an_altar

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Misanthrope — the white-bearded old man in a long black hooded cloak walking away across the empty field with his eyes down, while at the edge of the picture a hand reaches in behind him and cuts his red purse free, the faithful have vanished from among men, they lie to one another
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_misanthrope

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, The Conjurer — the gaping crowd leaning in over the trickster's table with its cups and little balls, the dupe bent double with his mouth open while the man in white beside him stares at the sky and quietly lifts his purse, they speak with flattering lips and a double heart, may the LORD cut off all flattering lips
pictures.name: pd_bosch_the_conjurer

pictures.scene: Lucas van Valckenborch, The Tower of Babel — the pale tower climbing ring on ring of arches into the sky, every tier crowded with sheds and cranes and tiny workmen, the harbour and the timber yards spread out at its foot and two small figures on the rock below pointing up at it, and every boastful tongue, with our tongues we will prevail
pictures.name: pd_valckenborch_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Pieter Brueghel the Younger, The Tax Collector's Office — the country people queued up hat in hand in the crowded office, one carrying a plucked bird, another a basket of eggs, under shelves stacked with ledgers and rows of hanging money bags, we own our lips who can be our master, for the cause of the oppressed
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_tax_collectors_office

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Beggars — the crippled men on the grass by the brick wall, one with his mouth open looking up and another dragging himself along on pads and crutches with foxtails pinned to his coat, a woman walking off behind them with the begging bowl, and for the groaning of the needy, I will now arise says the LORD
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_beggars

pictures.scene: Gerrit Dou, Old Woman Reading a Lectionary — the old woman in a fur cap and fur-collared cloak holding the heavy printed gospel book up close in both hands, her eyes down on the page and her whole face lit by it out of the dark, I will bring safety to him who yearns, the words of the LORD are flawless
pictures.name: pd_dou_old_woman_reading_a_lectionary

pictures.scene: Joseph Wright of Derby, An Iron Forge — the white-hot bar lying under the great water-driven hammer and throwing its light over the whole dark shed, the smith stooping to it with his tongs while the master stands by with folded arms and his wife and child watch from the shadow, like silver refined in a furnace, like gold purified sevenfold
pictures.name: pd_wright_an_iron_forge

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Sheepfold by Moonlight — the whole flock pressed together inside the hurdle fence on the dark plain, the low moon standing just above the horizon and laying a pale light along their backs, You O LORD will keep us, You will forever guard us from this generation
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_sheepfold_moonlight

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Netherlandish Proverbs — the crooked village where every folly is being acted out at once, the roof tiled with tarts, a man in armour belling the cat, one woman tying a blue cloak over her husband and another shearing a pig while her neighbour shears a sheep, the wicked wander freely, and vileness is exalted among men
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_netherlandish_proverbs

lines.text: For the choirmaster. According to Sheminith. A Psalm of David.
Help, O LORD, for the godly are no more;
the faithful have vanished from among men.
They lie to one another;
they speak with flattering lips and a double heart.
May the LORD cut off all flattering lips
and every boastful tongue.
They say, “With our tongues we will prevail.
We own our lips—who can be our master?”
“For the cause of the oppressed
and for the groaning of the needy,
I will now arise,” says the LORD.
“I will bring safety to him who yearns.”
The words of the LORD are flawless,
like silver refined in a furnace,
like gold purified sevenfold.
You, O LORD, will keep us;
You will forever guard us from this generation.
The wicked wander freely,
and vileness is exalted among men.
